name: How to Create an Automation
trigger: You just did (or are about to do) a process nobody else knows how to run, or someone asked you "how do I do X" for the second time.
purpose: Processes that live in one person's head break when that person is out. This is how every Automation at Build gets made: narrate the real process to Claude with the sop-creator skill installed. Nobody fills out a template by hand.
doneWhen: The Automation is live in the Automation Hub with your name at the top, and the link is in the relevant Slack channel if others run the process.

steps.title: Can you do the process live right now?
steps.trigger: Claude is open with the sop-creator skill installed.
steps.work: Narrating live is best because memory idealizes. If you cannot do it live, a voice memo transcript, Slack thread, or a typed rough description works, slightly worse. Otherwise wait until the next time you run the process.

steps.title: Do the process and narrate it to Claude
steps.trigger: You are about to run the process for real.
steps.work: Do the process and narrate as you go, like training someone over your shoulder. Include the ugly parts: workarounds, the one brand you handle differently, who you ping when stuck. Those become the Exceptions and escalation sections.

steps.title: Paste your notes or transcript into Claude
steps.trigger: You have a transcript, thread or rough description instead of a live run.
steps.work: Paste it into Claude and say "make this an Automation".

steps.title: Claude asks up to four short questions
steps.work: Claude asks for what is missing: trigger, failure cases, who to escalate to, owner. If Claude did not pick up that you want an Automation, say "use the sop-creator skill" directly.

steps.title: Answer, and Claude shows a draft
steps.work: Answer the questions. Claude shows a draft Automation in chat. For processes with real judgment calls (pricing exceptions, comping a customer), tell Claude who owns the decision so the Automation says "gather these facts and bring to [person]" rather than pretending the call is mechanical.

steps.title: Do the steps match what you actually did?
steps.work: Read the draft and check the steps against what you did. If it came out bloated, tell Claude "cut this down, plain language" before approving. Don't approve slop.

steps.title: Say publish; Claude posts it to the Automation Hub
steps.work: Claude publishes the page to the Automation Hub and gives you the link. If publishing to Notion fails, copy the draft into a new page in the Automation Hub, tag it, and tell Sam the connector broke. Later corrections go through Claude too ("in the receiving Automation, step 3 is now X"); it edits the existing page rather than duplicating.

steps.title: Share the link
steps.work: If other people run this process, drop the link in the relevant Slack channel.
